canDo.en: I can agree and disagree diplomatically in a meeting, soften my opinions, and discuss past decisions and their consequences with third and mixed conditionals.
canDo.bg: Мога дипломатично да се съглася или да не се съглася на среща, да смекчавам мнението си и да обсъждам минали решения и последиците им с трето и смесено условно изречение.

body.en: In English-speaking workplaces a flat "No, you're wrong" or "That's not true" usually sounds hostile, even when it is meant as a neutral correction. Speakers prefer to acknowledge the other view first and then disagree: "I see your point, but…", "I'm not sure I agree…", "I'm not entirely convinced…". Partial agreement is signalled with "up to a point" or "to some extent". Hedges like "perhaps", "I'd say" and "it might be worth…" make a proposal easier to accept. Bulgarian meetings tolerate more directness, so translating your Bulgarian tone word for word can make you sound rude.
body.bg: В англоезична работна среда рязкото "No, you're wrong" или "That's not true" обикновено звучи враждебно, дори когато е замислено като неутрална поправка. Хората първо признават другата гледна точка и после изразяват несъгласие: "I see your point, but…", "I'm not sure I agree…", "I'm not entirely convinced…". Частично съгласие се изразява с "up to a point" или "to some extent". Смекчаващи думи като "perhaps", "I'd say" и "it might be worth…" правят едно предложение по-лесно за приемане. На българските срещи прямотата е по-приемлива, затова ако превеждаш тона си дума по дума, може да прозвучиш грубо.

examples: I see your point, but I'm not sure the budget allows it.
I'd go along with that, up to a point.
I'm not entirely convinced that's the best option.
It might be worth asking the client first.

title.en: Third and mixed conditionals for regrets
title.bg: Трето и смесено условно за съжаления

body.en: The third conditional imagines a different past: If + past perfect, would have + past participle. "If we had tested it, we wouldn't have delayed the launch" (but we didn't test it, and we did delay). A mixed conditional links a different past to a different present: If + past perfect, would + base verb. "If we'd hired another developer, we wouldn't be so stressed now." For regrets and criticism without "if", use should have / could have + past participle: "We should have asked earlier." Bulgarian uses "ако бяхме…, щяхме да…" for both time frames, so pay attention to whether the result is in the past or the present.
body.bg: Третото условно изречение си представя различно минало: If + past perfect, would have + трето причастие. "If we had tested it, we wouldn't have delayed the launch" (но не сме тествали и сме забавили пускането). Смесеното условно свързва различно минало с различно настояще: If + past perfect, would + основна форма. "If we'd hired another developer, we wouldn't be so stressed now." За съжаление и критика без "if" използвай should have / could have + трето причастие: "We should have asked earlier." На български и за двата случая казваш "ако бяхме…, щяхме да…", затова внимавай дали резултатът е в миналото или в настоящето.

texts.title: Project review: the delayed app launch
paragraphs: Helen: Let's be honest about what went wrong. If we had tested the payment system properly in March, we wouldn't have had to delay the launch.
Raj: I see your point, but I'm not sure testing was the real issue. The client changed the requirements twice in April. Even if we had tested earlier, those changes would still have caused problems.
Helen: That's fair. Still, I think we could have pushed back on some of those changes.
Sofia: I'd go along with that, up to a point. Perhaps we should have agreed on a clear deadline for changes. If we'd done that, we wouldn't be working weekends now.
Raj: I'm not entirely convinced the client would have accepted that, to be honest. They're our biggest account, and if we had refused their changes, we might have lost them altogether.
Sofia: Maybe, but losing a bit of goodwill would have been better than losing three weekends.
Helen: Fair enough. Let's put it in the contract next time, then, and see how they react.

items.prompt: A colleague says: "We should cut the marketing budget by half." You disagree, but want to keep a good working relationship. What is the most appropriate reply?
options: You're wrong. That's a terrible idea.
I see where you're coming from, but I'm not sure halving it would help sales.
No. Marketing is important.
I disagree with you completely and totally.

explanation.en: Acknowledging the other view ("I see where you're coming from") and then hedging the disagreement ("I'm not sure…") is the standard diplomatic pattern. The other options are grammatical but blunt, and in an English-speaking meeting they would probably sound aggressive.
explanation.bg: Първо признаваш другата гледна точка ("I see where you're coming from"), после смекчаваш несъгласието ("I'm not sure…") — това е стандартният дипломатичен модел. Другите варианти са граматически верни, но твърде резки и на англоезична среща вероятно биха прозвучали агресивно.

hints.en: Look for an answer that first shows you understand the other person.
hints.bg: Потърси отговор, който първо показва, че разбираш другия.

items.sentence: If we had booked the venue earlier, we wouldn't ___ to pay so much.

explanation.en: This is a third conditional about an unreal past: If + had booked, would(n't) have + past participle. The participle of "have" is "had", so we get "wouldn't have had to pay". Learners often write "wouldn't had" — after "would" you always need the base form "have".
explanation.bg: Това е трето условно изречение за нереално минало: If + had booked, would(n't) have + трето причастие. Третото причастие на "have" е "had", така че става "wouldn't have had to pay". Често се греши "wouldn't had" — след "would" винаги трябва основната форма "have".

hints.en: The past participle of "have" is "had" — so you need two words.
hints.bg: Третото причастие на "have" е "had" — значи ти трябват две думи.

objective.en: Choose a mixed conditional for a present result.
objective.bg: Да избереш смесено условно за резултат в настоящето.

items.prompt: Choose the best ending: "If I had accepted that job in Berlin last year, I ___."
options: had lived in Germany now
will be living in Germany now
would live in Germany now
would have lived in Germany now

explanation.en: The condition is in the past (had accepted… last year), but the result is about now ("now"), so we need a mixed conditional: would + base verb. "Would have lived" refers to the past and clashes with "now". "Will" and "had lived" aren't possible in the result clause here.
explanation.bg: Условието е в миналото (had accepted… last year), но резултатът е за сега ("now"), затова трябва смесено условно изречение: would + основна форма. "Would have lived" е за миналото и не пасва на "now". "Will" и "had lived" не са възможни тук в главното изречение.

objective.en: Criticise a past decision with "should have".
objective.bg: Да критикуваш минало решение с "should have".

accept: We should have asked for more time.
Should we have asked for more time?

explanation.en: "Should have + past participle" expresses regret or criticism about the past: we didn't ask, and that was a mistake. Bulgarian says "Трябваше да поискаме", which leads learners to write "We had to ask" — but that means it was an obligation, and we did ask.
explanation.bg: "Should have + трето причастие" изразява съжаление или критика за миналото: не сме поискали и това е било грешка. На български казваш "Трябваше да поискаме", заради което учащите пишат "We had to ask" — но това значи, че е било задължително и сме го направили.

items.prompt: Your manager says: "We had to cancel the trip." What does this mean?
options: It was necessary to cancel the trip, and they cancelled it.
Cancelling the trip was a mistake.
They didn't cancel the trip, but they wanted to.
They might cancel the trip in the future.

explanation.en: "Had to" = it was necessary, and it happened. If cancelling had been a mistake, she would say "We shouldn't have cancelled the trip". Bulgarian "трябваше да" can mean both, so it's easy to confuse them.
explanation.bg: "Had to" = беше необходимо и се е случило. Ако отмяната беше грешка, тя би казала "We shouldn't have cancelled the trip". Българското "трябваше да" може да означава и двете, затова лесно се бъркат.

hints.en: "Had to" is about obligation, not regret.
hints.bg: "Had to" е за задължение, не за съжаление.

items.sentence: I agree with you up to a ___, but the costs are still too high.

explanation.en: "Up to a point" means "partly" — you agree with some of what was said, but not all. It's a useful way to disagree without sounding confrontational.
explanation.bg: "Up to a point" значи "донякъде" — съгласен си с част от казаното, но не с всичко. Полезен начин да не се съгласиш, без да звучиш конфликтно.

accept: I'm not entirely convinced it will work.

explanation.en: "I'm not entirely convinced…" is a polite way of saying "I don't think…". "Entirely" makes the doubt sound partial, which leaves room for discussion.
explanation.bg: "I'm not entirely convinced…" е учтив начин да кажеш "Не мисля, че…". "Entirely" прави съмнението да звучи частично и оставя място за обсъждане.

objective.en: Understand a speaker's argument in a meeting.
objective.bg: Да разбереш аргумента на говорещ на среща.

items.prompt: What is Raj's main point in his first turn?
options: The team tested the payment system too late.
Earlier testing would have prevented every problem.
The client should not have paid for the app.
The client's changes would have caused delays even with earlier testing.

explanation.en: Raj says: "Even if we had tested earlier, those changes would still have caused problems." He is questioning Helen's view that testing was the main cause.
explanation.bg: Raj казва: "Even if we had tested earlier, those changes would still have caused problems." Той поставя под въпрос мнението на Helen, че тестването е основната причина.

hints.en: Look at the sentence with "Even if".

objective.en: Interpret a mixed conditional in context.
objective.bg: Да тълкуваш смесено условно изречение в контекст.

items.prompt: Sofia says: "If we'd done that, we wouldn't be working weekends now." What does she imply?
options: The team didn't agree on a deadline, and as a result they're working weekends now.
The team agreed on a deadline, so they're not working weekends.
The team will have to work weekends in the future.
The team worked weekends in the past, but not now.

explanation.en: This is a mixed conditional: an unreal past (they didn't agree on a deadline) with a present result (they are working weekends now). "We'd done" here is "we had done", not "we would".
explanation.bg: Това е смесено условно изречение: нереално минало (не са се договорили за срок) с резултат в настоящето (сега работят през уикендите). "We'd done" тук е "we had done", а не "we would".

hints.en: Real situation: the opposite of the if-clause.
hints.bg: Реалната ситуация е обратното на if-частта.

objective.en: Identify the decision at the end of a meeting.
objective.bg: Да откриеш решението в края на среща.

items.sentence: At the end of the meeting, Helen suggests including a deadline for changes in the ___ next time.

explanation.en: Helen's last line: "Let's put it in the contract next time, then, and see how they react."
explanation.bg: Последната реплика на Helen: "Let's put it in the contract next time, then, and see how they react."
